name: Familial Keratoacanthoma

criteria.description: Presence of multiple keratoacanthoma lesions appearing simultaneously or sequentially
Positive family history of keratoacanthoma or similar skin tumors
Lesions demonstrate spontaneous regression within weeks to months
Histological confirmation showing well-differentiated squamous epithelioma with central keratin-filled crater
No evidence of invasive squamous cell carcinoma on biopsy

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of multiple keratoacanthoma lesions with positive family history and spontaneous regression, supported by histopathology
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic testing may support diagnosis but is not routinely available

laboratory: Histopathology showing well-differentiated squamous epithelioma with central keratin-filled crater
Absence of atypical mitoses or invasive carcinoma features
imaging: Not routinely required; dermoscopy may show central keratin plug and vascular patterns
genetic: Possible mutations in TGFBR1 gene reported in some familial cases
other: Clinical observation of lesion regression over time

distinguishingFeatures: Cysts are slow growing and lack central keratin-filled crater
Lesions are typically smaller, firm papules
No central keratin plug or crater

redFlags: Rapid lesion growth with ulceration and bleeding
Failure of lesions to regress spontaneously
Histopathological evidence of invasive squamous cell carcinoma
references: James WD, Berger TG, Elston DM. Andrews' Diseases of the Skin: Clinical Dermatology. 13th ed. Elsevier; 2019.
Harwood CA, Proby CM. Keratoacanthoma and squamous cell carcinoma: clinical and histopathological features. Clin Exp Dermatol. 2006.
